claim: Replay is safe: a repeated delivery of the same fact merges into the existing row instead of inserting a new one.
method: Read the Delta tables directly and count rows per idempotency_key, then reconcile against the MERGE metrics in the transaction log.

merge_reconciliation.reads: MERGE was offered 47 source rows across 20 commits but inserted only 29 rows and updated 18 in place. Offered minus inserted is the duplicate work the merge key absorbed - that gap is the replay safety, measured rather than asserted.

why_it_holds: integration_tasks.dedupe_latest collapses a batch to one event per idempotency_key before the MERGE ever runs, picking the max of (occurred_at, event_id) so the winner does not depend on Kafka delivery order.
The Delta MERGE then matches on idempotency_key (delta_store.MERGE_KEY), so a duplicate that survives into a later batch updates the existing row instead of inserting.
Table version may still advance on a replay - a commit happened - while the row count does not. Those are different facts and IT-J2 asserts both.
